key_insight: Intensity-modulated photoluminescence spectroscopy (IMPLS) measures perovskite charge-carrier lifetime directly under operating-like injection levels, overcoming the ambiguity of conventional time-resolved methods.
engineering_relevance: IMPLS can separate charge transfer from interface recombination in perovskite solar-cell stacks, providing a more actionable diagnostic for device and interface optimization.
method: Use frequency-domain photoluminescence instead of time-domain lifetime fitting.
Measure lifetime at a defined injection level, including one-sun-equivalent illumination.
Apply a transfer-function model for stacks to disentangle transport and recombination effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that IMPLS matches steady-state photoluminescence on thin films, reveals more complex responses in stacks, and detects a third characteristic frequency in devices where IMVS is often limited by capacitive effects.
watch_item: The extracted lifetime in full devices depends on a transfer-function interpretation, so capacitive and interfacial effects must be modeled carefully to avoid misattribution.
paper_title: Operando Charge Carrier Dynamics by Intensity-Modulated Photoluminescence: From Perovskite Thin Films to Solar Cells
